role: Operator runbook for production incidents: per-category symptoms and actions (AI provider outage, CloudKit failure, crash spike, encryption key loss, HealthKit data errors, privacy leak suspicion, transitive-dependency CVE) plus a post-incident note template.
toplevel: Markdown only; no executable content. References code symbols (FeatureFlags, EncryptionManager.getOrCreateKey/keychainAccount/reEncryptIfNeeded, CloudPayloadCodec, SleepBoundaryResolver, AppFactResolver, ProviderConsentTracker), the make target sendable-guard, docs/runbooks/hotfix.md, .github/dependabot.yml open-pull-requests-limit and the iCloud container iCloud.com.chrissharp.flowrecovery; all of these exist in the repo (Constants.swift:12, Emuqu.entitlements:23, Makefile:58, .github/dependabot.yml:24).

units.does: no behavioural claim: title and preamble telling the operator to pick the matching section.

units.key: § Runbook: Incident Response > A. AI provider outage / breaking change
units.does: Claims the per-provider kill switch lives in FeatureFlags (Settings -> Flo), is per-device with no remote config, so a provider can be disabled for everyone only by shipping a build; providers live in Sources/Assistant/Providers/ and implement a small AIProvider protocol. Code matches: FeatureFlags keys providerOpenAIEnabled..providerDeepSeekEnabled in app-group defaults (Constants+SleepAndDisplay.swift:422-475), protocol AIProvider at Emuqu/Sources/Assistant/Providers/AIProvider.swift:494.

flags.text: A build that changes a provider's FeatureFlags default does not turn the provider off for every user: FeatureFlags.value(for:) returns the stored UserDefaults value whenever one exists and uses defaultValue only when nothing is stored, and the Settings -> Flo toggle writes an explicit Bool on every flip. Anyone who ever toggled that provider (off then back on) keeps an explicit true, so the shipped default-off build leaves the provider enabled on their device. The runbook's 'a build is the only way to turn it off for everyone' is therefore insufficient; the build must also clear or override the stored key.

units.key: § Runbook: Incident Response > B. CloudKit sync failure (zone-wide)
units.does: CloudKit outage triage: check CloudKit Dashboard for container iCloud.com.chrissharp.flowrecovery, deploy schema to production if only this container fails, never mass-reset user state. Container id matches Constants.swift:12 and Emuqu.entitlements:23; schema-not-deployed failure mode is the one CloudKitSessionFreshness.noteSaveFailure logs ("not in the production schema").

units.key: § Runbook: Incident Response > C. Crash spike
units.does: Crash-spike triage: symbolicate from App Store Connect/dSYM, read code at the crashing line, run make sendable-guard, hotfix via hotfix.md. make sendable-guard exists (Makefile:58) and docs/runbooks/hotfix.md exists. Listed common causes are prose, not tied to code.

units.key: § Runbook: Incident Response > D. Encryption key loss
units.does: Encryption key loss triage: device not unlocked since reboot (archive key is AfterFirstUnlock), iCloud Keychain sync of the synchronizable CloudPayloadCodec key (one Keychain item per key; log line 'waiting for its backup key to sync'), restore without Keychain loses the archive key, then Delete All My Data (type DELETE MY DATA). For wide-scale failures inspect EncryptionManager.getOrCreateKey(version:), keychainAccount(for:) per version, and add a previous-version fallback modeled on reEncryptIfNeeded. Code: accessibility kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock (EncryptionManager.swift:252), per-key accounts 'cloud-payload-key-id-' (CloudPayloadCodec.swift:76), log line at CloudKitSyncManager+Pull.swift:305, confirm phrase at DeleteAllDataPage.swift:28.

flags.text: Step 3-4 says a key-version bump without migration makes old files unreadable and that a hotfix must add a fallback to try the previous key version. decrypt already reads the version byte from each blob and loads that version's key (EncryptionManager.swift:99-106, extractVersion :148, loadKey :188), so old files stay readable as long as the old Keychain item exists; decryption does not go through getOrCreateKey at all. reEncryptIfNeeded has no caller (comment EncryptionManager.swift:25-27). An operator following the runbook would look for the wrong failure mechanism.

units.key: § Runbook: Incident Response > E. Apple Health data corruption
units.does: HealthKit data-corruption triage: suspect DST/time-zone math in SleepBoundaryResolver and addingTimeInterval patterns, reproduce with the user's date, hotfix with a regression test. SleepBoundaryResolver exists (Emuqu/Sources/Analysis/SleepBoundaryResolver.swift:52).

units.key: § Runbook: Incident Response > F. Privacy / leak suspicion
units.does: Privacy-leak triage: treat as P0; verify AppFactResolver sends only aggregates (no raw RR or sample timestamps); verify ProviderConsentTracker gates provider calls; pull the diagnostic log via More -> Settings -> Troubleshooting -> Export Diagnostic Log; if real, ship a build with that provider's FeatureFlags default off and update SECURITY.md. Code: the only rrSeries use in Facts is nadirWallClock deriving one timestamp (AppFactResolver+Sleep.swift:412-418); consent gate consentGateAllowsDispatch runs before dispatch; Export Diagnostic Log button at SettingsPages+DiagnosticActions.swift:53; SECURITY.md lives at .github/SECURITY.md.

flags.text: Step 5 says 'File a SECURITY.md update'; there is no SECURITY.md at the repository root, only .github/SECURITY.md, so the instruction names a file location that does not exist as written.

A build that changes a provider's FeatureFlags default does not turn the provider off for every user: FeatureFlags.value(for:) returns the stored UserDefaults value whenever one exists and uses defaultValue only when nothing is stored, and the Settings -> Flo toggle writes an explicit Bool on every flip. Anyone who ever toggled that provider (off then back on) keeps an explicit true, so the shipped default-off build leaves the provider enabled on their device. Step 5's 'a build is the only way to turn it off for everyone' is therefore insufficient; the build must also clear or override the stored key.

Step 4 says the exported diagnostic log confirms what was actually sent to the provider. Export Diagnostic Log shares only the debugLogger file (DiagnosticLogExport -> debugLogger.exportToFileAsync), whose lines are PHI-scrubbed (health values replaced with <redacted>) and which never logs request payloads. The record of what was sent is LLMRequestAudit: an in-memory FIFO of 10 entries, lost on relaunch, viewable only in LLMPromptAuditView and not part of any export. An operator following the runbook cannot confirm or rule out a leak from the artifact it names.

units.key: § Runbook: Incident Response > G. CVE against a transitive dependency you cannot bump
units.does: Transitive-dependency CVE playbook: Zip arrives via polar-ble-sdk, yyjson and swift-* via WhisperKit; establish reachability, ship a build with the path off (no runtime flag for the sensor path; voice degrades to typed input), file upstream, bump by hand because Dependabot open-pull-requests-limit: 0 blocks version PRs only. Package.resolved lists polar-ble-sdk, whisperkit, yyjson, zip and swift-* packages; .github/dependabot.yml:24,36 sets open-pull-requests-limit: 0.

flags.text: Runbook says the swift-* packages arrive through WhisperKit; the repo's own SBOM generator records swift-protobuf as arriving through polar-ble-sdk (with Zip). A swift-protobuf advisory triaged by this runbook would be scoped to the voice path (degrade to typed input) when the reachable consumer is the BLE sensor path, so step 2 would switch off the wrong subsystem.

Runbook says that with the WhisperKit path off, voice degrades to typed input. In code WhisperKit is an opt-in STT provider; Apple SFSpeechRecognizer is the default and the documented fallback when WhisperKit fails to load or transcribe, and non-English locales already route to Apple. Turning the WhisperKit path off leaves voice working via Apple Speech, so the user-facing message the runbook prescribes overstates the loss.

units.does: no behavioural claim: post-incident note template (what broke, detection time, root cause, why CI missed it, prevention, TTD/TTM/TTF).
